dermal filler injections hurt?","tab_content":"

          Most patients describe filler injections as brief pressure rather than sharp pain. We apply a topical numbing cream first, and most FDA-approved hyaluronic acid fillers also contain lidocaine, a local anesthetic that numbs as we work. Sensitive areas like the lips may feel more, so we adjust pacing and numbing to keep you comfortable.<\/p>"},{"_id":"e5b0b5f","tab_title":"How long do dermal fillers last?","tab_content":"

          Most hyaluronic acid fillers last 9 to 18 months, depending on the area treated and the product used. High-movement areas like the lips tend to break down filler faster than the cheeks or jawline. At your follow-up we track how your result holds so you can plan touch-ups on your own schedule.<\/p>"},{"_id":"99b3411","tab_title":"What is the downtime after fillers?","tab_content":"

          Plan for minor swelling or redness at the injection sites for 24 to 48 hours. Most patients return to work the same day. We ask you to avoid strenuous exercise, alcohol, and firm pressure on the treated area for the first day so the filler settles evenly.<\/p>"},{"_id":"fe5df0e","tab_title":"Can dermal fillers be reversed?","tab_content":"

          Yes. Hyaluronic acid fillers can be dissolved with hyaluronidase, an enzyme injected into the treated area if you want to adjust or remove your result. This reversibility is a key safety advantage of hyaluronic acid fillers, and one reason we use them as our standard at the Irving clinic.<\/p>"},{"_id":"f3ae4db","tab_title":"Can I get Botox and fillers in the same visit?","tab_content":"

          Yes. Botox relaxes the muscles that create expression lines, while fillers restore volume in a different layer of tissue. Because the two treatments work in different ways, they can be done safely in the same appointment. Many patients combine them for a complete refresh in one visit.<\/p>"},{"_id":"d5e94f1","tab_title":"How much do dermal fillers cost in Irving?","tab_content":"

          Dermal fillers at our Irving clinic cost $800 for one syringe or $1,520 for two syringes. class=\"ihw-container\"><h2>How Botox Works<\/h2><p class=\"ihw-science-lead\"> Botox is the brand name for onabotulinumtoxinA, a purified neuromodulator FDA-approved for cosmetic use since 2002. Micro-injections temporarily block signals between nerve and muscle, allowing the overlying skin to smooth out. <\/p><div class=\"ihw-science-grid\"><article class=\"ihw-science-card\"><div class=\"ihw-science-icon\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0 32 32\" width=\"36\" height=\"36\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"2\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\"><path d=\"M22 4l6 6-4 4-6-6 4-4z\"\/><path d=\"M18 8L4 22v6h6L24 14\"\/><path d=\"M14 12l6 6\"\/><\/svg><\/div><span class=\"ihw-science-phase\">Phase 01<\/span><h3>The Mechanism<\/h3><div class=\"ihw-science-stat\">Targets one muscle at a time<\/div><p> Botulinum toxin type A blocks acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction. The muscle relaxes; the wrinkle softens. Surrounding expression stays intact. <a href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK557921\/\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">NCBI clinical reference<\/a>. <\/p><\/article><article class=\"ihw-science-card\"><div class=\"ihw-science-icon\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0 32 32\" width=\"36\" height=\"36\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"2\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\"><circle cx=\"16\" cy=\"16\" r=\"12\"\/><path d=\"M16 8v8l5 3\"\/><\/svg><\/div><span class=\"ihw-science-phase\">Phase 02<\/span><h3>Onset and Duration<\/h3><div class=\"ihw-science-stat\">Visible by day 10, lasts 3-4 months<\/div><p> Initial smoothing begins around day 3 to 4. Full effect appears by day 10 to 14. Most patients see 3 to 4 months of result before the muscle gradually regains function. <\/p><\/article><article class=\"ihw-science-card\"><div class=\"ihw-science-icon\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><svg viewBox=\"0 0 32 32\" width=\"36\" height=\"36\" fill=\"none\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"2\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\"><path d=\"M16 3L5 7v8c0 7 5 13 11 14 6-1 11-7 11-14V7l-11-4z\"\/><path d=\"M11 16l4 4 7-8\"\/><\/svg><\/div><span class=\"ihw-science-phase\">Phase 03<\/span><h3>Safety Profile<\/h3><div class=\"ihw-science-stat\">23+ years of clinical use<\/div><p> With more than two decades of cosmetic use, Botox has one of the most extensively studied safety profiles in aesthetic medicine. Side effects are rare and typically mild when administered by a trained medical practitioner, consistent with <a href=\"https:\/\/www.aad.org\/public\/cosmetic\/wrinkles\/botox-treatment-overview\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">American Academy of Dermatology safety guidance<\/a>. <\/p><\/article><\/div><\/div><\/section><style> Timeline<\/span><h2>What to Expect Day by Day After Your Botox Treatment<\/h2><p class=\"ihw-bx-sub\">Most pages tell you Botox takes \"3 to 7 days\" to show. The real timeline is more nuanced. Here is exactly what happens at each stage so you know what is normal and when to call us.<\/p><div class=\"ihw-bx-flow\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><span>Day 0<\/span><span class=\"dot\"><\/span><span class=\"line\"><\/span><span>Day 3-7<\/span><span class=\"dot\"><\/span><span class=\"line\"><\/span><span>Day 10-14<\/span><span class=\"dot\"><\/span><span class=\"line\"><\/span><span>Month 1-3<\/span><span class=\"dot\"><\/span><span class=\"line\"><\/span><span>Month 3-4<\/span><\/div><div class=\"ihw-bx-timeline-grid\"><article class=\"ihw-bx-stage\"><span class=\"marker\">Day 0<\/span><h3>Treatment Day<\/h3><p>Injection takes 10 to 15 minutes. Avoid lying down or vigorous exercise for 4 hours.<\/p><\/article><article class=\"ihw-bx-stage\"><span class=\"marker\">Day 3 to 4<\/span><h3>First Muscle Relaxation<\/h3><p>Treated muscles begin to relax. This is the earliest a non-clinician might detect a change.<\/p><\/article><article class=\"ihw-bx-stage\"><span class=\"marker\">Day 5 to 7<\/span><h3>Visible Smoothing Begins<\/h3><p>Friends and family often start commenting around this window. Dynamic wrinkles soften noticeably. Patients typically describe feeling lighter in the treated areas, like the muscles are resting.<\/p><\/article><article class=\"ihw-bx-stage\"><span class=\"marker\">Day 10 to 14<\/span><h3>Full Effect & Touch-Up Window<\/h3><p>Peak neuromodulator effect. This is the window where patients photograph results and feel most confident about the investment.<\/p><\/article><article class=\"ihw-bx-stage\"><span class=\"marker\">Month 3<\/span><h3>First Signs of Return<\/h3><p>Subtle muscle activity begins to reappear, especially in highly expressive patients. Some dynamic movement returns before any visible lines. Time to schedule your next consultation.<\/p><\/article><article class=\"ihw-bx-stage\"><span class=\"marker\">Month 3 to 4<\/span><h3>Time to Re-Treat<\/h3><p>Most patients schedule re-treatment in this window. Treating before complete return often means future treatments need fewer units, because treated muscles gradually weaken with consistent disuse.<\/p><\/article><article class=\"ihw-bx-stage\"><span class=\"marker\">Beyond 4 Months<\/span><h3>What If You Skip?<\/h3><p>Muscles return to baseline function. Wrinkles return gradually, not worse than before. Years of consistent treatment may reduce baseline static lines because treated muscles slightly atrophy with disuse.<\/p><\/article><\/div><\/div><\/section><section class=\"ihw-section\" style=\"text-align:center;\"><div class=\"ihw-container\"><span class=\"ihw-section-eyebrow\">Clinical & Regulatory Track Record<\/span><h2>Botox Cosmetic: Two Decades of FDA-Cleared Use<\/h2><p class=\"ihw-bx-sub\">Botulinum toxin type A is one of the most studied molecules in aesthetic medicine. Below is a synthesized timeline of FDA milestones and US treatment volume, with sources you can verify.<\/p><div class=\"ihw-bx-table-wrap\"><table class=\"ihw-bx-table\"><thead><tr><th>Year<\/th><th class=\"col-mile\">Milestone<\/th><th>Clinical Detail<\/th><th>Source<\/th><\/tr><\/thead><tbody><tr><td class=\"year\">1989<\/td><td>FDA approval of botulinum toxin type A for medical use (strabismus and blepharospasm)<\/td><td>First therapeutic use established years before cosmetic application<\/td><td class=\"src\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.accessdata.fda.gov\/scripts\/cder\/daf\/index.cfm?event=overview.process&ApplNo=103000\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">FDA Drugs@FDA<\/a><\/td><\/tr><tr><td class=\"year\">2002<\/td><td>FDA approval for cosmetic use on glabellar lines (the \"11\" lines between brows)<\/td><td>Foundational cosmetic indication; based on Phase III randomized controlled trials<\/td><td class=\"src\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.accessdata.fda.gov\/scripts\/cder\/daf\/index.cfm?event=overview.process&ApplNo=103000\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">FDA Drugs@FDA<\/a><\/td><\/tr><tr><td class=\"year\">2013<\/td><td>Approval extended to lateral canthal lines (crow's feet)<\/td><td>Second cosmetic indication after a decade of off-label use<\/td><td class=\"src\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.accessdata.fda.gov\/scripts\/cder\/daf\/index.cfm?event=overview.process&ApplNo=103000\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">FDA Drugs@FDA<\/a><\/td><\/tr><tr><td class=\"year\">2017<\/td><td>Approval extended to forehead lines (horizontal lines)<\/td><td>Third cosmetic indication. Most commonly treated area today<\/td><td class=\"src\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.accessdata.fda.gov\/scripts\/cder\/daf\/index.cfm?event=overview.process&ApplNo=103000\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">FDA Drugs@FDA<\/a><\/td><\/tr><tr><td class=\"year\">2024<\/td><td>9.5+ million neurotoxin treatments performed in the US in a single year<\/td><td>Botulinum toxin type A remains the #1 minimally invasive cosmetic procedure for the 23rd consecutive year<\/td><td class=\"src\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.plasticsurgery.org\/news\/plastic-surgery-statistics\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">ASPS Statistics<\/a><\/td><\/tr><tr><td class=\"year\">2025<\/td><td>Average first-time cosmetic neurotoxin patient is 35 years old<\/td><td>Preventative (\"baby\") Botox starting in late 20s drives demographic shift<\/td><td class=\"src\"><a href=\"https:\/\/www.aafprs.org\/Media\/Press_Releases\/\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">AAFPRS Census<\/a><\/td><\/tr><\/tbody><\/table><\/div><p class=\"ihw-bx-tablefoot\">Synthesized from public FDA, American Society of Plastic Surgeons, and American Academy of Facial Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery data.<\/p><\/div><\/section><section class=\"ihw-section\" style=\"background:#f9faf9;text-align:center;\"><div class=\"ihw-container\"><span class=\"ihw-section-eyebrow\">Common Misconceptions<\/span><h2>Botox Myths vs Clinical Facts<\/h2><p class=\"ihw-bx-sub\">Six misconceptions we field at every Irving consultation, answered with the clinical references behind each correction.<\/p><div class=\"ihw-bx-myth-grid\"><article class=\"ihw-bx-myth\"><div class=\"ihw-bx-myth-head\"><span class=\"pill\">Myth<\/span><p>\"Botox is dangerous because it's a toxin.\"<\/p><\/div><div class=\"ihw-bx-fact-body\"><span class=\"pill\">Fact<\/span><p>Botulinum toxin type A used cosmetically is purified, FDA-cleared since 2002, and administered in micro-doses (typically 10 to 30 units per area). Each unit contains nanogram-level quantities of active protein, far below any threshold for systemic concern when administered by a trained clinician.<\/p><span class=\"src\">Source: <a href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK557921\/\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">NCBI StatPearls clinical reference<\/a><\/span><\/div><\/article><article class=\"ihw-bx-myth\"><div class=\"ihw-bx-myth-head\"><span class=\"pill\">Myth<\/span><p>\"Botox will make my face look frozen or expressionless.\"<\/p><\/div><div class=\"ihw-bx-fact-body\"><span class=\"pill\">Fact<\/span><p>Frozen results come from over-dosing or imprecise injection placement, not from Botox itself. Anatomy-mapped dosing by a Board Certified clinician produces selective muscle relaxation while preserving natural expression. Our 2-week follow-up exists specifically to catch any asymmetry early.<\/p><span class=\"src\">Source: <a href=\"https:\/\/www.aad.org\/public\/cosmetic\/wrinkles\/botox-treatment-overview\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">American Academy of Dermatology guidance<\/a><\/span><\/div><\/article><article class=\"ihw-bx-myth\"><div class=\"ihw-bx-myth-head\"><span class=\"pill\">Myth<\/span><p>\"If I stop Botox, my wrinkles will come back worse than before.\"<\/p><\/div><div class=\"ihw-bx-fact-body\"><span class=\"pill\">Fact<\/span><p>Stopping Botox returns muscles to baseline function. Wrinkles return gradually over 3 to 4 months, not worse than they were originally. Long-term consistent use can actually reduce baseline static lines because treated muscles atrophy slightly with disuse.<\/p><span class=\"src\">Source: <a href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK557921\/\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">NCBI clinical review on neuromodulator pharmacology<\/a><\/span><\/div><\/article><article class=\"ihw-bx-myth\"><div class=\"ihw-bx-myth-head\"><span class=\"pill\">Myth<\/span><p>\"Botox is only for older women.\"<\/p><\/div><div class=\"ihw-bx-fact-body\"><span class=\"pill\">Fact<\/span><p>The average first-time cosmetic neurotoxin patient is 35 years old. Preventative or \"baby\" Botox in the late 20s is increasingly common and trains muscles before deep static lines form. Men account for roughly 7% of treatments and that share is growing yearly.<\/p><span class=\"src\">Source: <a href=\"https:\/\/www.aafprs.org\/Media\/Press_Releases\/\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">AAFPRS Annual Census<\/a><\/span><\/div><\/article><article class=\"ihw-bx-myth\"><div class=\"ihw-bx-myth-head\"><span class=\"pill\">Myth<\/span><p>\"More units mean better results.\"<\/p><\/div><div class=\"ihw-bx-fact-body\"><span class=\"pill\">Fact<\/span><p>Optimal results come from matching dose to specific muscle strength, not from maximizing units. Most forehead patients need 10 to 20 units, glabellar 15 to 25, crow's feet 10 to 15 per side. Over-dosing produces frozen expressions, not better smoothing.<\/p><span class=\"src\">Source: <a href=\"https:\/\/www.accessdata.fda.gov\/scripts\/cder\/daf\/index.cfm?event=overview.process&ApplNo=103000\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">FDA Botox prescribing information<\/a><\/span><\/div><\/article><article class=\"ihw-bx-myth\"><div class=\"ihw-bx-myth-head\"><span class=\"pill\">Myth<\/span><p>\"Telehealth Botox is the same as in-clinic.\"<\/p><\/div><div class=\"ihw-bx-fact-body\"><span class=\"pill\">Fact<\/span><p>Botox requires an in-person injection by a trained clinician. No legitimate telehealth provider ships Botox for self-injection because the procedure requires anatomy mapping, sterile administration, and immediate clinician oversight for adverse events. Any service claiming otherwise is operating outside FDA-cleared protocols.<\/p><span class=\"src\">Source: <a href=\"https:\/\/www.aad.org\/public\/cosmetic\/wrinkles\/botox-treatment-overview\" target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\">AAD patient safety guidance<\/a><\/span><\/div><\/article><\/div><\/div><\/section><section class=\"ihw-section ihw-steps\"><div class=\"ihw-container\"><h2>What to Expect at Your Appointment<\/h2><p class=\"ihw-steps-sub\"> From consultation to follow-up, here is exactly how your Botox visit unfolds. <\/p><div class=\"ihw-steps-list\"><article class=\"ihw-step\"><div class=\"ihw-step-num\">1<\/div><span class=\"ihw-step-time\">15-20 MIN<\/span><h3>Consultation<\/h3><p>Lori reviews your aesthetic goals, medical history, and any prior injectable experience. Photos taken for baseline.<\/p><\/article><article class=\"ihw-step\"><div class=\"ihw-step-num\">2<\/div><span class=\"ihw-step-time\">5-10 MIN<\/span><h3>Anatomy Mapping<\/h3><p>Your facial muscles are mapped at rest and in motion. This determines exact injection points and unit dosing per area.<\/p><\/article><article class=\"ihw-step\"><div class=\"ihw-step-num\">3<\/div><span class=\"ihw-step-time\">10-15 MIN<\/span><h3>Injection<\/h3><p>Precise microdoses are administered with a fine needle. Most patients describe each injection as a brief pinch.<\/p><\/article><article class=\"ihw-step\"><div class=\"ihw-step-num\">4<\/div><span class=\"ihw-step-time\">2 WEEKS<\/span><h3>Follow-Up<\/h3><p>Complimentary review at the 2-week mark. Cookie Policy

This Cookie Policy explains how Irving Health and Wellness Clinic uses cookies and similar technologies when you visit our website.

Last updated: December 22, 2025

COOKIE CONSENT

By continuing to use our website, you consent to our use of cookies in accordance with this Cookie Policy. You can manage your cookie preferences at any time through your browser settings.

1. What Are Cookies?

Cookies are small text files that are placed on your device (computer, smartphone, or tablet) when you visit a website. They are widely used to make websites work more efficiently and provide information to website owners.

Cookies help us understand how you use our website, remember your preferences, and improve your overall experience. They can be "session cookies" (deleted when you close your browser) or "persistent cookies" (remain on your device until deleted or expired).

2. Types of Cookies We Use

Irving Health and Wellness Clinic uses several types of cookies to enhance your experience on our website:

Cookie Type Purpose Duration
Strictly Necessary Cookies Essential for website functionality, security, and navigation. These cannot be disabled. Session
Performance Cookies Help us understand how visitors interact with our site by collecting anonymous data. 1-2 years
Functional Cookies Remember your preferences and choices to provide enhanced features. 1 year
Targeting/Advertising Cookies Used to deliver relevant advertisements and track campaign effectiveness. 1-2 years

Strictly Necessary Cookies

These cookies are essential for our website to function properly. They enable core functionality such as:

  • Secure login and authentication
  • Appointment booking system functionality
  • Shopping cart and checkout processes
  • Security and fraud prevention
  • Load balancing to ensure website stability

Without these cookies, services you have requested cannot be provided. These cookies do not gather information about you for marketing purposes.

Performance and Analytics Cookies

These cookies collect information about how visitors use our website, including:

  • Which pages are visited most often
  • Time spent on different pages
  • Error messages received
  • How users navigate through the site

This information is aggregated and anonymous. We use services like Google Analytics to help us improve website performance and user experience.

Functional Cookies

These cookies allow our website to remember choices you make and provide enhanced, personalized features:

  • Remembering your login details (if you choose)
  • Storing your preferences for appointment types
  • Remembering language or region preferences
  • Customizing content based on your previous visits

Targeting and Advertising Cookies

These cookies are used to deliver advertisements that are relevant to you and your interests. They may be set by our advertising partners and are used to:

  • Build a profile of your interests
  • Show relevant ads on other websites you visit
  • Measure the effectiveness of advertising campaigns
  • Limit the number of times you see an advertisement

These cookies do not store directly personal information but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and device.

3. Third-Party Cookies

In addition to our own cookies, we use various third-party services that may set cookies on your device. These include:

Google Analytics

We use Google Analytics to understand how visitors interact with our website. Google Analytics uses cookies to collect anonymous information including the number of visitors, where visitors have come from, and the pages they visited. This helps us improve our website and services.

For more information about Google Analytics cookies, visit Google's Privacy Policy.

Social Media Plugins

Our website includes social media features (such as Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter buttons) that may set cookies to enable you to share content. These features may collect your IP address and which page you're visiting, and may set a cookie to enable the feature to function properly.

Advertising Networks

We may work with third-party advertising networks to display ads on our website or to manage our advertising on other sites. These partners may use cookies to collect information about your activities to provide you with targeted advertising.

4. Managing Your Cookie Preferences

You have the right to decide whether to accept or reject cookies. You can exercise your cookie preferences in several ways:

Browser Settings

Most web browsers allow you to control cookies through their settings. You can set your browser to:

  • Block all cookies
  • Block third-party cookies only
  • Delete cookies when you close your browser
  • Alert you when a website tries to set a cookie

Instructions for managing cookies in popular browsers:

  • Google Chrome: Settings, then Privacy and Security, then Cookies and other site data
  • Safari: Preferences, then Privacy, then Manage Website Data
  • Firefox: Options, then Privacy & Security, then Cookies and Site Data
  • Microsoft Edge: Settings, then Privacy, Search, and Services, then Cookies

Opt-Out Tools

You can opt out of interest-based advertising by visiting:

  • Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA): www.aboutads.info/choices
  • Network Advertising Initiative (NAI): www.networkadvertising.org/choices
  • Google Ads Settings: www.google.com/settings/ads

Impact of Disabling Cookies

Please note that if you disable or refuse cookies, some parts of our website may become inaccessible or not function properly. Specifically, you may not be able to:

  • Book appointments online
  • Save your preferences
  • Access certain personalized features
  • Use shopping cart functionality

5. Mobile Devices

If you access our website through a mobile device, you can manage cookies through your device settings:

  • iOS: Settings, then Safari, then Block All Cookies
  • Android: Settings, then Privacy, then Clear browsing data

Mobile apps may also use mobile identifiers for advertising and analytics. You can manage these through your device's privacy settings or opt out of personalized advertising.

6. Do Not Track Signals

Some browsers include a "Do Not Track" (DNT) feature that signals to websites that you do not want to have your online activity tracked. Currently, there is no industry standard for how to respond to DNT signals.

Our website does not currently respond to DNT signals. However, you can use the cookie management tools described above to control tracking on our site.

7. Children's Privacy

Our website is not intended for children under 13 years of age. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children through cookies or any other means. If you are a parent or guardian and believe your child has provided us with information, please contact us immediately.

8. Updates to This Cookie Policy

We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time to reflect changes in technology, legislation, our business operations, or for other operational, legal, or regulatory reasons.

When we make changes, we will update the "Last Updated" date at the top of this policy. We encourage you to review this Cookie Policy periodically to stay informed about how we use cookies.

If we make material changes to this policy, we may notify you by posting a notice on our website homepage or by sending you an email (if you have provided your email address).

9. Your Rights Under Privacy Laws

Depending on your location, you may have certain rights regarding cookies and personal data:

  • Right to Access: Request information about what data has been collected through cookies
  • Right to Deletion: Request deletion of data collected through cookies
  • Right to Opt-Out: Opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information
  • Right to Non-Discrimination: Exercise your rights without discrimination

For more information about your privacy rights, please see our Privacy Policy or contact us using the information below.

10. Contact Us

If you have questions or concerns about this Cookie Policy or how we use cookies, please contact us:

Irving Health and Wellness Clinic is committed to protecting your privacy. This document includes our Notice of Privacy Practices for your health information (Part 1) and our website Privacy Policy (Part 2).

Effective: June 24, 2026  |  Last updated: June 24, 2026

NOTICE OF PRIVACY PRACTICES

THIS NOTICE DESCRIBES HOW MEDICAL INFORMATION ABOUT YOU MAY BE USED AND DISCLOSED AND HOW YOU CAN GET ACCESS TO THIS INFORMATION. PLEASE REVIEW IT CAREFULLY.

Part 1 – Notice of Privacy Practices (Your Health Information)

This part applies to protected health information (PHI), the health and treatment information you share with us as a patient. It is separate from the website data practices in Part 2.

Our pledge regarding your health information

We are required by law to keep your protected health information private and secure, to give you this notice of our legal duties and privacy practices, to notify you if a breach compromises your information, and to follow the terms of the notice currently in effect.

How we may use and disclose your health information without your authorization

  • Treatment. To provide and coordinate your care, such as your provider reviewing your labs, history, and goals to build a treatment plan.
  • Payment. To bill and collect payment for services, such as providing an itemized superbill for your HSA, FSA, or insurer.
  • Health care operations. For quality improvement, training, scheduling, and general clinic operations.
  • Appointment reminders and communications. To contact you by phone, text, or email about appointments and the services we offer, consistent with your preferences.
  • As required by law. When federal, state, or local law requires it, such as public health reporting or a valid court order.
  • To prevent a serious threat to health or safety.

Uses that require your written authorization

The following require your prior written authorization, which you may revoke at any time in writing: marketing communications beyond our own permitted service communications, any sale of your PHI, most uses of psychotherapy notes if applicable, and any other use not described in this notice.

Your rights regarding your health information

  • Inspect and copy your health and billing records. We may charge a reasonable, cost-based fee for copies.
  • Request an amendment if you believe your records are incorrect or incomplete.
  • Request an accounting of certain disclosures we have made.
  • Request restrictions on how we use or disclose your PHI.
  • Request confidential communications, such as contact only at a certain phone number or address.
  • Receive a paper copy of this notice at any time.
  • Revoke an authorization you previously gave, in writing, except where we have already acted on it.

Complaints

If you believe your privacy rights have been violated, you may contact our Privacy Officer at (972) 891-8650 or info@irvingwellnessclinic.com, or file a complaint with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office for Civil Rights, 200 Independence Avenue SW, Washington, D.C. 20201, 1-877-696-6775, www.hhs.gov/ocr. You will not be penalized or retaliated against for filing a complaint.

Changes to this notice

We reserve the right to change this notice and to make the revised notice effective for information we already have as well as information we receive in the future. The current notice will be posted in the clinic and on our website with its effective date.

Part 2 – Website Privacy Policy

This part explains what we collect through irvingwellnessclinic.com and how we use it. It applies to online activity on this website only and does not cover the health information practices in Part 1 or any information collected offline.

Information we collect

  • Information you give us through contact and booking forms: your name, email, phone number, and the contents of your message.
  • SMS opt-in data if you provide your phone number and check the consent box.
  • Automatically collected log data such as IP address, browser type, ISP, date and time, and referring pages. This is used in aggregate to analyze trends and administer the site and is not linked to your identity.
  • Cookies to operate the site and understand usage. You can disable cookies in your browser settings.

How we use this information

To operate and improve the website, respond to your inquiries, schedule and confirm appointments, send communications you have requested, and protect against fraud and misuse.

SMS and text messaging

You opt in by submitting your phone number and checking the consent box. Message frequency varies, and message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out at any time. We do not share mobile opt-in information or consent with any third parties or affiliates for marketing purposes.

Cookies, analytics, and advertising

We may use analytics tools to understand site usage. If we use third-party advertising or remarketing services, those providers may set their own cookies, which we do not control. We recommend reviewing those providers' own privacy policies. We do not sell your personal information.

Your privacy rights (CCPA and GDPR)

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict, or port your personal data, and to object to certain processing. To exercise these rights, contact us using the details below, and we will respond within the timeframe required by applicable law.

Children's privacy

Our website and services are not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. If you believe a child has provided us information, contact us and we will delete it.

Data security

We use reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect the information we hold. No method of transmission or storage is fully secure, but we work to protect your information and limit access to authorized personnel.

Contact us

Irving Health and Wellness PLLC
Phone: (972) 891-8650  |  Email: info@irvingwellnessclinic.com  |  Website: irvingwellnessclinic.com

Terms & Conditions

These conditions govern your use of Irving Health and Wellness Clinic. By accessing our site and services, you agree to be bound by these terms.

Last updated: 8/22/24

HIPAA'S NOTICE

In accordance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA), we are required to give you a Notice of our legal duties and privacy practices. Please see our Privacy Policy for more information.

1. Acceptance of Terms

By accessing and using irvingwellnessclinic.com(the Site) or utilizing our services, you agree to be bound by these Terms and Conditions. If you do not agree with any part of these terms, please do not use our services.

If you do not agree to any of these terms, you are not authorized to use our site. We reserve the right to modify these terms at any time. Your continued use of our services after any changes constitutes your acceptance of the modified terms.

2. Medical Services & Treatment

Not Emergency Services

Irving Health and Wellness Clinic is not an emergency medical facility or a replacement for emergency services. If you are experiencing a medical emergency, please call 911 immediately.

Services we offer include but are not limited to:

  • IV Hydration and vitamin infusion therapy
  • Medical weight loss programs
  • Hormone health evaluations and treatment
  • Aesthetic services and facials
  • Recovery treatments
  • NAD IV therapy
  • PRP hair treatment (Mermit)

Medical Evaluation

All treatments require a medical evaluation and consultation to determine suitability. Treatments may not be appropriate for all patients. We reserve the right to refuse services if you do not meet the criteria or if your health condition contraindicates treatment.

3. Appointment Policies

Scheduling

Appointments can be booked online via our website, by phone at (972) 891-8650, or through our patient portal. We recommend booking in advance to secure your preferred time slot.

Cancellation Policy

We require at least 24 hours' notice for any changes or cancellations:

  • 24 hours or more in advance: No cancellation fee
  • Less than 24 hours notice: 50% of service cost
  • No-shows: Full service charge may be applied to your account

Late Arrivals

Please arrive 10-15 minutes before your appointment time. Late arrivals may result in shortened service time or the need to reschedule, and you may be charged for the missed appointment.

4. Payment Terms

Payment Methods

We accept cash, credit cards, debit cards and electronic payment methods. Payment is due at the time of service unless other arrangements have been made in advance.

Insurance

Insurance is accepted only for services covered by your policy. However, many services (like IV therapy, aesthetic treatments, and wellness programs) are elective and typically not covered by insurance. You are responsible for verifying your coverage prior to treatment.

Package Deals and Memberships

  • Package discounts reflect a lower rate
  • Services must be used within the specified timeframe
  • No refunds on packages once purchased
  • Packages are non-transferable
  • Fee is non-refundable unless we cancel a service (either directly or through a provider)

Refund Policy

All sales are final unless you cancel before receiving service (per our cancellation policy). If we are unable to provide a service as promised or at all, you are entitled to a full refund, less a processing fee or charges incurred.

5. Informed Consent & Risks

Treatment Risks

All medical and aesthetic treatments carry some level of risk. We will discuss risks with you prior to treatment, and you will be required to sign consent forms acknowledging these risks.

Post-visit Actions

You are responsible for following all post-treatment instructions. Failure to do so may impact your results and could increase the risk of complications. Please contact our office if you have questions or experience unexpected symptoms.

Emergency Procedures

In the event of an emergency during treatment, we will take appropriate steps including calling 911 if needed. By using our services, you consent to emergency treatment if necessary.

6. Liability & Indemnification

Limitation of Liability

To the fullest extent permitted by law, Irving Health and Wellness Clinic and its staff are not liable for any indirect, incidental, consequential, or punitive damages arising from your use of our services or website. This includes, but is not limited to:

  • Adverse reactions or complications from treatment
  • Failure to disclose medical information or allergies
  • Failure to follow pre- or post-treatment instructions
  • Loss of income or business due to complications

Professional Documents

All documents, including medical records and treatment plans, may only be released after final settling of your account and with signed authorization. Our services are personal to you and may not be assigned or transferred.

Refusal to Authorize or Sign

If you refuse to sign consent forms or other required documentation, you will not be able to receive the requested treatment until such documentation is completed.

7. Conduct & Facility Rules

Respectful Behavior

We maintain a professional environment. We expect our patients to treat staff with respect and courtesy. Abusive, threatening, or inappropriate behavior will not be tolerated and may result in termination of services and removal from the facility.

Prohibited Activities

  • Smoking or vaping anywhere on our premises
  • Arrival under the influence of drugs or alcohol
  • Use of offensive or abusive language
  • Taking photos or videos of staff or other patients without permission
  • Unauthorized recording of consultations or treatments

Right to Refuse Service

We reserve the right to refuse service to anyone for any reason, including but not limited to: failure to comply with clinic policies, inappropriate behavior, or situations where we believe treatment may not be in your best interest medically.

8. Intellectual Property

Website Content

All content on our website, including text, logos, images, and graphics, is protected by copyright and trademark laws. You may not copy, reproduce, or distribute any material from our site without prior written consent.

User-Generated Content

If you provide us with content, such as reviews or testimonials, you grant us a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, and distribute that content for promotional purposes. You retain ownership of your content.

Photography & Marketing

Before and after photos or testimonials require your separate written consent. We will not use images or testimonials for marketing without your explicit permission. You have the right to revoke consent at any time.

9. Dispute Resolution

Informal Resolution

We encourage patients to first try to resolve any disputes or concerns directly with our management. Please contact us at (972) 891-8650 or email info@irvingwellnessclinic.com.

Binding Arbitration

If we cannot resolve a dispute informally, you agree to submit the issue to binding arbitration under the rules of the American Arbitration Association.

Legal Jurisdiction

These Terms and Conditions are governed by the laws of the State of Texas. Any legal action must be brought in Dallas County, Texas. If any part of these Terms is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall remain in full force and effect.

Class Action Waiver

You agree that disputes will be handled on an individual basis and waive any right to participate in a class action lawsuit or class-wide arbitration.

10. Termination of Services

Patient-Initiated Termination

You may discontinue services at any time. However, certain packages, memberships, or services may require written notice and are non-refundable once services have been provided or initiated.

Clinic-Initiated Termination

We reserve the right to discontinue services to any patient for reasons including but not limited to: failure to follow treatment plans, missed appointments, non-payment, or inappropriate behavior. We will provide written notice if services are terminated.

Medical Records

Upon request, we will transfer your medical records to your new provider in accordance with applicable laws, following settlement of any outstanding balances.

Questions About These Terms?

If you have questions or concerns about our Terms and Conditions, please don't hesitate to reach out. We're here to help clarify anything you need.

Irving Health and Wellness Clinic

Medically reviewed by Lori Secerovic, APRN, FNP-C, MSN, Lead Practitioner.

Irving Health and Wellness Clinic is a simple idea, done well. You should be able to walk into a place that feels calm, get real medical guidance, and leave with a plan that makes sense. Not a lecture. Not a confusing list of upsells.

We are based in Irving, TX, and our team brings 17+ years of combined experience in wellness care and medical aesthetics. Some people come in for a specific goal: weight loss, energy, skin, confidence. Others come in because they feel off and want a second set of eyes. Both are normal. We work with you from there.

","align":"center","typography_typography":"custom","typography_font_family":"Montserrat","typography_font_size":{"unit":"px","size":16,"sizes":[]},"_element_width":"initial","_element_custom_width":{"unit":"px","size":800,"sizes":[]}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"},{"id":"dcaa2e7","elType":"widget","settings":{"tabs":[{"_id":"aboutfaq1","tab_title":"How long is the first appointment?","tab_content":"

Plan for 45 minutes for your initial consultation. We review your history, current concerns, and goals before discussing options. Most patients leave with a clear protocol and a timeline for results. Same-week openings are usually available.

"},{"_id":"aboutfaq2","tab_title":"Do you accept insurance?","tab_content":"

Most wellness services are paid out of pocket. We provide itemized superbills for HSA and FSA submission, which many of our patients use. Our team can explain what your plan typically covers before any treatment, so there are no surprises.

"},{"_id":"aboutfaq3","tab_title":"Do I need a referral?","tab_content":"

No referral is needed for any service we offer. Every visit is by appointment, and the fastest way to book your first one is the booking link or a call to 972-891-8650.

"},{"_id":"aboutfaq4","tab_title":"Are your protocols evidence-based?","tab_content":"

Yes. Every treatment plan follows published clinical guidance from organizations including the Endocrine Society and the American Academy of Dermatology. Lori reviews each plan personally before treatment begins.

"},{"_id":"aboutfaq5","tab_title":"How is your clinic different from a typical med spa?","tab_content":"

Our clinic is medically supervised and led by a Board-Certified Family Nurse Practitioner with 17+ years of clinical experience. Standard med spas often skip the clinical workup. We start with labs and goals, then build the plan around your biology rather than a fixed menu.

"},{"_id":"aboutfaq6","tab_title":"What conditions do you address most often?","tab_content":"

Chronic fatigue, perimenopausal hormone shifts, low testosterone, stubborn weight that resists diet and exercise, brain fog, sluggish thyroid function, and skin concerns like fine lines, hyperpigmentation, and acne scarring. Each protocol is tailored to your specific labs and history.

"},{"_id":"aboutfaq7","tab_title":"What should I bring to my first visit?","tab_content":"

Bring a photo ID, any current medication list, recent lab results if you have them, and a short note with your top two or three goals. The goals note matters more than people expect; it keeps the conversation focused.

"},{"_id":"aboutfaq8","tab_title":"Will my information stay private?","tab_content":"

Yes. Your health records, lab work, and visit notes are handled under HIPAA-aligned data practices. We never share patient information with third parties for marketing or any other reason. Records are accessible only to your care team.

"},{"_id":"aboutfaq9","tab_title":"Are you accepting new patients?","tab_content":"

Yes. We welcome new patients across all service lines and accept same-week first appointments when capacity allows. Booking is available online at our scheduling page or by calling 972-891-8650 during business hours, Monday through Friday.
